children: By Wayne Cole
Asian share markets slipped on Monday as unease over AI's enormous funding needs undermined confidence ahead of a week packed with earnings, while the euro eased in the wake of rioting across France.

A fall in oil prices offered some support to bonds and Wall Street stock futures, limiting Asia's losses. Oil fell following US President Donald Trump's decision to waive some sanctions on Russia, though he later said a final decision on the matter had not been made.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday that the president would take up to 60 days to assess the economic impact of such a move. Brent futures
still fell 1.6% to $108.06 a barrel, while US crude futures
lost 0.7% to $100.70 a barrel.
Meanwhile, Iran reported another tanker had hit a mine in the Strait of Hormuz.
Geopolitical tensions combined with safe-haven flows from equities to extend a rally in sovereign bonds, with 10-year Treasury yields down 3 basis points at 5.0645%
, having just recorded their largest weekly fall in over eight months.
All of this helped S&P 500 futures
edge up 0.5%, while Nasdaq futures
rose 0.8%.
Asian markets were hampered by concerns about tech; Japan's Nikkei
fell 2.0% after losing 5.4% last week as the tech sector took a beating. South Korea
dropped 1.6%, having shed more than 14% last week.
MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MIAPJ0000PUS) eased 0.3%.

"Investors have long worried that AI revenues won't be sufficient to recoup the massive upfront investment, while AI infrastructure may need to be written down as it ages and depreciates in the meantime, which lowers book value massively," said My Bui, an economist at fund manager AMP.
"Rising government bond yields and wider corporate credit spreads are increasing financing costs, making it harder to borrow, refinance, and keep the AI infrastructure build-out going."
A LOT RIDING ON EARNINGS
The PHLX Semiconductor Index shed 11.4%
last week in its longest losing streak since 2008.
Investors will be hoping Meta
will beat Wall Street forecasts when it reports earnings on Wednesday, along with semiconductor firms Lam Research
and Texas Instruments
and Elon Musk-led companies SpaceX
and Tesla
Meta is one of five AI hyperscalers that combined are expected to increase their capital spending to about $1.2 trillion next year, according to Goldman Sachs.
Others reporting include Netflix
, Procter & Gamble
, General Motors
and GE Aerospace
Earnings are still expected to rise 30% overall thanks to the huge profits made by tech firms.
European stocks were weighed down by political uncertainty in France with EUROSTOXX 50 futures
off 0.4%, while DAX futures
lost 0.3% and FTSE futures
were flat.
Those same concerns saw the euro ease 0.2% to $1.1212
, nearer to last week's 16-month low of $1.1113.
The dollar dipped 0.1% against the yen to 157.75
and has spent the entire month so far in a tight range as the threat of Japanese intervention has kept speculative sellers at bay.
In commodity markets, non-interest-bearing gold got a lift from falling yields and rose 0.4% to $4,181 an ounce
